text:
Ava: quick follow-up from the pricing section  dropping a short thread for clarifications on credits, quotas, and demo spikes. please paste customer snippets.
Rohit: customer Q: we did a live demo and credits disappeared fast. how do we prevent surprise usage?
Maya: short: streaming + tool calls = prompt + streamed tokens + tool outputs. many small streams add per-request overhead. best practice: batch responses or use longer single streams for demos.
Priya: can support issue time-limited demo keys that cap qps and total credits?
Maya: yes. Support can create demo keys with a per-second cap and a total credit allowance. include demo date, expected concurrency, and sample prompts in the request.
Kenji: ops detail: default when a route exceeds quota -> 429 with Retry-After header and an `x-rw-quota-token`. Dedicated customers can enable short queuing (3-10s) or automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant.
Rohit: are grace bursts free?
Maya: grace bursts consume credits. we auto-apply a small graceburst for accounts in good standing once per billing period; larger temporary increases require Support.
Priya: what about mid-cycle top-ups? prorated?
Maya: one-off top-ups prorate into the remaining billing period. recurring monthly credits apply at cycle start. committed/reserved credits follow contract terms.
Kenji: SDKs emit a client event `rate_limit.hit` and surface Retry-After. we plan to ship a helper that implements jittered exponential backoff and token-bucket-friendly retry in the next SDK milestone.
Ava: action items: (1) Maya to publish a short KB with streaming token examples & a calc tool by EOD tomorrow, (2) Kenji to add SDK backoff helper to sprint, (3) Support to share demo key request template.
support-bot: demo-key template: https://intranet.redwood/support/templates/demo-key-request (link)
Rohit: thanks everyone. i'll collect these into the KB; drop follow-ups here. :thumbsup:
